# Keycloak 2FA Messaging Authenticator

> A Keycloak SPI plugin that adds messaging-based OTP two-factor authentication.
> Supports SMS (Twilio, AWS SNS, Vonage), Telegram, WhatsApp, and Signal.
> Compatible with Keycloak 26.x. Requires Java 21+.

## Installation

- Download JAR from Maven Central or GitHub Releases
  - groupId: io.github.mesutpiskin
  - artifactId: keycloak-2fa-messaging-authenticator
  - version format: <plugin-version>-KC<keycloak-version> (e.g. 26.0.0-KC26.6.1)
- Copy JAR to <KEYCLOAK_HOME>/providers/
- Run: <KEYCLOAK_HOME>/bin/kc.sh build
- Restart Keycloak

## Authentication Flow Configuration

- Keycloak admin → Authentication → Flows → duplicate Browser flow
- Add "Messaging OTP" execution inside the Forms sub-flow
- Set requirement: REQUIRED (all users) or use "Conditional Messaging OTP" (condition-based)
- Bind the new flow as the Browser flow

Provider IDs:

- messaging-authenticator — authenticator, "Messaging OTP"
- messaging-conditional-authenticator — authenticator, "Conditional Messaging OTP"
- messaging-authenticator-setup — required action, "Set up Messaging Authenticator"

## Authenticator Settings (⚙️ on the Messaging OTP row)

- message.channel: SMS | TELEGRAM | WHATSAPP | SIGNAL (default SMS)
- sms.provider: twilio | aws-sns | vonage (default twilio, only used when channel is SMS)
- otp.length: 6 digits (default)
- otp.ttl: 300 seconds (default)
- otp.resend.cooldown: 60 seconds (default)
- otp.max.attempts: 5 (default) — incorrect attempts before the code is invalidated
- simulation.mode: false — when true, logs the OTP to server output instead of sending (dev only)
- skip.setup: true — users whose contact attribute is already populated skip enrollment

## Provider Credentials

- TWILIO: twilio.accountSid + twilio.authToken + twilio.fromNumber (E.164)
- AWS_SNS: aws.region (e.g. us-east-1) + aws.accessKeyId + aws.secretAccessKey
  - IAM principal needs sns:Publish on resource "*"
  - static credentials only; instance profiles and IRSA are not used
  - new AWS accounts are in the SMS sandbox and only reach verified numbers
  - SNS enforces a monthly SMS spending limit, USD 1.00 by default
- VONAGE: vonage.apiKey + vonage.apiSecret + vonage.fromNumber (sender ID or E.164)
- TELEGRAM: telegram.bot.token
- WHATSAPP: whatsapp.api.url (Cloud API messages endpoint) + whatsapp.api.token
  + whatsapp.from.number (E.164)
- SIGNAL: signal.cli.rest.url (base URL of signal-cli-rest-api) + signal.from.number (E.164)

## Recipient User Attributes

The contact address is read from a user attribute, configurable per channel:

- sms.contact.attribute — default phoneNumber (E.164)
- telegram.contact.attribute — default telegramChatId
- whatsapp.contact.attribute — default phoneNumber
- signal.contact.attribute — default phoneNumber

## Source Layout

- src/main/java/                                — authenticator SPI implementation
- src/main/java/.../service/impl/               — one MessageSender per provider
- src/main/resources/META-INF/services/         — ServiceLoader descriptors, including
                                                  com.mesutpiskin.keycloak.auth.messaging.service.MessageSender
- src/main/resources/theme-resources/templates/ — FreeMarker forms (OTP entry, setup, verify)
- src/main/resources/theme-resources/messages/  — i18n properties (en, tr)

## Extending

Implement com.mesutpiskin.keycloak.auth.messaging.service.MessageSender in a separate JAR and
register it under META-INF/services/com.mesutpiskin.keycloak.auth.messaging.service.MessageSender

## Troubleshooting

- Authenticator missing from the admin console: confirm the JAR is in providers/ and that
  kc.sh build was run after copying it.
- No OTP delivered: check message.channel and sms.provider, the provider credentials, and that
  the user attribute exists in the expected format. Set simulation.mode=true to confirm the flow
  independently of the provider.
- ServiceConfigurationError naming a MessageSender and "Unable to get public no-arg constructor":
  the sender's dependencies are absent from the classpath, not a constructor fault.
